summary: Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992) at Minobusan Junior College, and in 1996 was attested as professor at Minobusan University and director at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Hoong Teik Toh specializes in Tibetology, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University by 2004, studying under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Cambridge and SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden, he taught at King's College Bangkok, directed the Greater-India Research Committee (~1934–1941), and served as vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1947–1968).

Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital. He held posts at the Calcutta Mint, Asiatic Society, and East India Company Library, and served as Boden Professor of Sanscrit at Oxford (1831–1860).

Horace L. Friess was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. After earning his bachelor's degree at Columbia and studying at Heidelberg, he spent his career at Columbia University (~1919–1966), also holding a post at Johns Hopkins University.

Horst Lasic specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999, where he became a lecturer in 1999, and served as a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1995.

Hosakote Krishna Sastri was an Indian epigraphist and scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1891–1925) and was Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925).
Hoseok Leigh specializes in philosophy and religious studies. Leigh studied under Ha-u Kim and earned a Doctor of Philosophy degree from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).
Hoseong Kim works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo and was attested as a professor at Dongguk University in 2011.
Hoshu Mitsuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1982) and was later attested as professor emeritus there in 2004.

Hoyo Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Rissho University (~1952–1961), where he later served as professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (~1978–2004) and as dean of the faculty (attested 1984–1985).
Hozen Seki was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hrachia Adjarian was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, the University of Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann, and under Antoine Meillet. He taught at Aramiyan School, Sanasarian College, and Yerevan State University (1923).

Hsiao-Lan Hu was a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD from Temple University, Hu served as associate professor of Religious Studies and Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun was a Buddhist figure who founded Fo Guang Shan, Buddha's Light International Association, and several colleges, serving as Fo Guang Shan abbot (~1967–1985). He studied under teachers including Zhikai and Yin Shun, and taught at Tunghai University.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

Hsu Yun was a Buddhist master and religious figure who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. He founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1953, serving as its honorary president that same year.

Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua was a Buddhist master who studied under Chang Chih and Hsu Yun. He founded the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, serving as its abbot (~1976–1995), along with the Buddhist Text Translation Society and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.
Hsueh-li Cheng is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Ohio University (~1974–1978) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (~1978–2014).
